The queue is not the problem

By Dana Okafor, 14 March 2026

We spent a week adding workers. The backlog kept growing, and the graph that mattered never moved. The queue was never the constraint: one row lock was, and every worker we added waited on it.

What we measured

Latency at the ninety ninth percentile went from 1,338 ms to 396 ms after a single change, and the change was not in the queue.

A number from one run is not a measurement. We ran it twelve times.

The lock was taken in claim.sql and held for the whole transaction, including the network round trip to the object store. Moving the upload out of the transaction was four lines.

What we would do first next time

  1. Look at where time is spent before adding anything.
  2. Ask what the workers are waiting on, not how many there are.
  3. Keep the run that disproved the theory.

None of this is new. It was still faster to add workers than to read the transaction, which is why we did the wrong thing for a week.
